final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package with 75% RVC, 18% labor-value content, indexed Mexican wage floor with independent auditor verification of union certification, Canadian dairy quotas (155K cheese/85K yogurt), and a five-year sunset with affirmative extension. Congress committed to vote within the week; all three parties locked final text language.
minority_objections: Supply-chain manufacturers raised unresolved concern about default-renew vs. hard-sunset mechanics at month 48
Mexico initially resisted independent auditor verification of union certification as sovereignty issue before accepting compromise language
key_conflicts: Mexico vs. U.S./Canada on independent auditor verification of union certification (resolved via compromise language confirming Mexican authorities' certification)
Canada vs. U.S. on audit structure sovereignty (resolved via joint quarterly audits with Mexican courts enforcing)
Labor union vs. USTR on labor-value floor percentage (resolved at 18% compromise from initial 15%/20% positions)
key_concessions: Mexico accepted independent auditor verification of union certification within quarterly audit cycle
Canada opened dairy quotas at 155K metric tons cheese, 85K yogurt with five-year lock
U.S. moved from 15% to 18% labor-value content floor
All parties accepted five-year sunset with affirmative extension instead of auto-renew or hard termination
red_lines: Mexico: union certification mechanism must confirm Mexican labor authorities' determinations, not override them
Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement preservation (mentioned but not contested in this meeting)
U.S. Congress: hard metric-ton dairy floors and independent labor enforcement verification required for ratification
Labor union: 18% minimum labor-value content with indexed wage floor and auditor verification
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Supply-chain adjustment costs and timeline uncertainty for retooling to 18% labor-value content
Default-renew vs. hard-sunset mechanics at month 48 left ambiguous despite supply-chain manufacturer's explicit question
Compliance cost and audit infrastructure burden on smaller suppliers
Political risk of Canadian Parliament ratification despite minister's confidence
downstream_risk_variables: Month-48 extension vote mechanics and bar for affirmative renewal
Operational definition of 'independent auditors' for union certification verification
Phase-in compliance costs for auto suppliers transitioning to 18% labor-value content
Canadian dairy sector political backlash to 155K/85K quota concessions
Congressional ratification timeline pressure (vote within one week)
uncertainty_notes: Supply-chain manufacturer's question about default-renew vs. hard-sunset at month 48 was never answered; the exact bar and process for affirmative extension vote remains undefined. Auto industry's demand for written clarification on phase-in timing was acknowledged but final text details not confirmed in transcript.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC and 18% labor-value content were core negotiation points that drove multiple rounds of back-and-forth; auto industry demanded written phase-in timeline and RVC thresholds locked before committing; USTR's proposal approval explicitly tied to resolving auto rules tension
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Labor enforcement mechanism (independent auditor verification, indexed wage floor, quarterly audits with benefit suspension) was the primary driver of R3-R4 negotiations; Congress stated 'Congress won't ratify a deal where we audit wages but have no independent eyes on union certification'; labor union threatened endorsement withdrawal; final package explicitly conditioned on locked labor text
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Dairy quotas (155K cheese/85K yogurt) were explicitly named by dairy_ag and us_congress as required for Congressional ratification; Canada's concession on these specific metric-ton floors was a key unlock for final package approval; dairy_ag stated 'that's where my government sees real value in a trilateral package'
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Chapter 19 mentioned once by canada_min as preserved in package but never contested or negotiated; no evidence it shaped outcomes
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Five-year sunset with affirmative extension was explicitly negotiated as compromise between hard termination and auto-renew; supply_chain_mfr stated 'My members won't build new lines or lock in suppliers if they're planning for a deal that expires'; sunset framework lock was condition for mexico_neg and ustr proposal approvals
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress explicitly stated ratification constraints drove labor enforcement demands and dairy quota floors; us_congress committed to vote 'within the week' and stated 'Congress votes on ratification the minute we leave this room'; labor union threatened to tell AFL-CIO deal doesn't protect workers; ratification risk drove multiple concessions
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Supply-chain manufacturers raised compliance cost, audit infrastructure, and retooling concerns multiple times but these did not block or redirect the negotiation; concerns were acknowledged ('my members can absorb compliance cost') but package moved forward without addressing operational details
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: Mexico explicitly used bilateral-first as leverage: 'You either shape that timeline with us now, or you're explaining to your auto sector why they're out of the deal'; 'commit to the audit structure now, or we're moving forward without you'; this pressure drove Canada's acceptance of audit structure and dairy concessions
